Brazil's second slice, and the dedicated Brazilian-fiscal-reporting session `G.63.md`/`G.64.md` item 10 called for (untouched across four hand-offs, `G.63.md` through `G.66.md`, before this session). Deliberately narrow, per `Research.1.md` §8's one-item-at-a-time discipline and `br-fpm-population.json`'s own deferred entry 2 ("this deserves the dedicated Brazilian-fiscal-reporting session entry already calls for, where it would sit alongside a proper LC 101/2000 node rather than floating alone"): one statute (Lei Complementar 101/2000, the Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal / LRF) and the two transparency instruments it names and structures, the Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária (RREO) and the Relatório de Gestão Fiscal (RGF). Brazil's national accounts, CPI, and the state-level FPE chain remain out of scope, as `br-fpm-population.json`'s entry 4 already flagged; so does state- and municipal-level RREO/RGF publication (thousands of individual reports) — this file builds the Union-level instruments and the statute that governs every level, not a census of who publishes them.

reports.title: Lei Complementar nº 101, de 4 de maio de 2000 (Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal — LRF)
reports.description: Brazil's Fiscal Responsibility Law, binding the Union, the states, the Federal District and every municipality (Art. 1º). Chapter IX, "Da Transparência, Controle e Fiscalização", names the corpus's two Brazilian budget-transparency instruments in one sentence — Art. 48 caput lists as instruments of fiscal-management transparency "os planos, orçamentos e leis de diretrizes orçamentárias; as prestações de contas e o respectivo parecer prévio; o Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária e o Relatório de Gestão Fiscal" — and then defines each one's structure and deadline in the articles that follow (Arts. 52–53 for the RREO, Arts. 54–55 for the RGF). The Constitution names the RREO independently at Art. 165 §3 ("O Poder Executivo publicará, até trinta dias após o encerramento de cada bimestre, relatório resumido da execução orçamentária"), so the LRF is the implementing statute for a constitutional obligation, not its sole origin — the same shape as `br-lei-8443` sitting under Art. 159 I of the Constitution in the FPM chain. One-off foundational instrument per `Research.1.md` §4 (Thomas's 2026-08-08 ruling): adopted once and amended in place since (most visibly by Lei Complementar 178/2021 and other later LCs touching individual articles), not reissued as a new instrument, so no `releases_per_year` is given.

reports.title: Relatório Resumido da Execução Orçamentária (RREO)
reports.publisher: Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (STN) / Poder Executivo
reports.description: The consolidated budget-execution summary every Poder Executivo (Union, state, Federal District, municipal) must publish, covering every branch of government under it. Art. 52 caput, quoted directly: the report "abrangerá todos os Poderes e o Ministério Público, será publicado até trinta dias após o encerramento de cada bimestre". Art. 53 lists what must accompany it — a verbatim, itemised methodology, not a description: "Acompanharão o Relatório Resumido demonstrativos relativos a: I - apuração da receita corrente líquida, na forma definida no inciso IV do art. 2º, sua evolução, assim como a previsão de seu desempenho até o final do exercício; II - receitas e despesas previdenciárias a que se refere o inciso IV do art. 50; III - resultados nominal e primário; IV - despesas com juros, na forma do inciso II do art. 4º; V - Restos a Pagar, detalhando, por Poder e órgão referido no art. 20, os valores inscritos, os pagamentos realizados e o montante a pagar". Independently, the 1988 Federal Constitution states the same publication obligation at Art. 165 §3: "O Poder Executivo publicará, até trinta dias após o encerramento de cada bimestre, relatório resumido da execução orçamentária." Published nationally through SICONFI (Sistema de Informações Contábeis e Fiscais do Setor Público Brasileiro) and made public via the Tesouro Transparente portal for the Union-level report used as this node's primary source.
reports.cadence_note: Bimonthly by statute — Art. 52 caput and Constitution Art. 165 §3 both fix the deadline at 30 days after the close of each two-month period, six editions per fiscal year.

reports.title: Relatório de Gestão Fiscal (RGF)
reports.publisher: Secretaria do Tesouro Nacional (STN) / Poderes e órgãos referidos no art. 20 da LRF
reports.description: The companion report to the RREO, comparing each branch of government's own fiscal management against the LRF's legal limits rather than summarising budget execution. Art. 54 caput, quoted directly: "Ao final de cada quadrimestre será emitido pelos titulares dos Poderes e órgãos referidos no art. 20 Relatório de Gestão Fiscal", signed in turn by the Chefe do Poder Executivo, the Legislature's Mesa Diretora, the Judiciary's Conselho de Administração, and the Ministério Público's Chefe (incisos I–IV) — a formally attested document, not a routine statistical release. Art. 55 caput and inciso I define its required content: "O relatório conterá: I - comparativo com os limites de que trata esta Lei Complementar, dos seguintes montantes:" — personnel expenses, consolidated and floating (mobiliária) debt, guarantees granted, and credit operations, per the alíneas that follow. Named alongside the RREO in Art. 48 caput as one of the LRF's transparency instruments (see `br-lc-101-2000`). Published through SICONFI, with the Union-level report used as this node's primary source.
reports.cadence_note: Quadrimestral by statute (Art. 54 caput) — issued at the close of each four-month period, three editions per fiscal year (end of April, August and December for the calendar-year fiscal year), independently confirmed via Tesouro Transparente's own descriptive text. Art. 63 of the LRF is reported elsewhere as granting municipalities under 50,000 inhabitants relief to a semi-annual schedule instead; not independently quoted this session, so not used to adjust this node's cadence.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY. Art. 52 caput establishes the RREO's scope and deadline ("abrangerá todos os Poderes e o Ministério Público, será publicado até trinta dias após o encerramento de cada bimestre"), and Art. 53's five incisos define its exact required content — including a cross-reference to the LRF's own definition of net current revenue ("receita corrente líquida, na forma definida no inciso IV do art. 2º") and to Art. 4º and Art. 50 for the interest and social-security demonstratives. This is genuine methodology, not merely a publication mandate — the report's structure and defined terms come from the statute itself, distinguishing this edge from `br-ibge-estimativas-populacao -> br-lei-8443` in `br-fpm-population.json`, which that file's own basis explicitly typed as `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on` because Lei 8.443 "compels the publication and fixes its deadline, and supplies no method." LC 101/2000 Arts. 52–53 supply the method.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY. Art. 48 caput names the RGF, alongside the RREO, as one of the LRF's own transparency instruments. Art. 54 caput fixes who issues it and on what cadence ("Ao final de cada quadrimestre será emitido pelos titulares dos Poderes e órgãos referidos no art. 20 Relatório de Gestão Fiscal"), and its parágrafo único and incisos I–IV fix who signs it. Art. 55 caput and inciso I define the report's actual content as a comparison against the LRF's own legal limits ("comparativo com os limites de que trata esta Lei Complementar") — the limits themselves, and the definitions used to test compliance against them, are set elsewhere in the same statute, making this methodology rather than a bare publication mandate.

_dropped.edge: State- and municipal-level RREO/RGF publications, individually
_dropped.why: Deliberately out of scope. The LRF binds every Union, state, Federal District and municipal Poder Executivo to publish its own RREO and RGF — thousands of individual reports, one per federative entity, all following the same statutory structure this file documents once at the Union level. Building every entity's own report as a separate node would multiply nodes without adding a new documented dependency; the methodology edge is already captured once, at the statute. Matches `br-fpm-population.json` entry 4's own scope discipline ("this slice is one chain deliberately").
